test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Roshan and Anshu together invested ₹13,500 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹9,000, Roshan's share was ₹1,300. What was Roshan's investment?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio = investment ratio

Roshan : Anshu = 1300 : (9000 − 1300) = 1300 : 7700 = 13 : 77

Total parts = 90

Roshan’s investment = (13/90) × 13500

**∴ Answer = ₹1950**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = 13500, Total profit = 9000, Roshan’s profit = 1300

**Formula used:**

Investment ratio = Profit ratio

**Calculation:**

⇒ Anshu’s profit = 9000 − 1300 = 7700

⇒ Ratio = 1300 : 7700 = 13 : 77

⇒ Total ratio = 13 + 77 = 90

⇒ Value of 1 part = 13500 ÷ 90 = 150

⇒ Roshan’s investment = 13 × 150 = 1950

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1950.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Rule

Profit share ∝ Investment when time is same.

Ratio Simplification

Reduce ratios to simplest form.

Unitary Method

Find value of one part to compute required value.

Profit Split

Total profit = sum of individual shares.
